newsitem.title: UK: Aviation insurance losses rise in 1996 - ILU.
newsitem.headline: Aviation insurance losses rise in 1996 - ILU.

text.p: The number of western-built jet airliners that declared total losses last year rose to 25 from 20 in 1995, the Institute of London Underwriters (ILU) said in a statement on Tuesday.

The estimated cost of total and major partial losses for western-built jets rose to $477 million from $418 million in 1995, added the ILU, which represents many of the leading international insurers operating in the London Market.
The year was one of the worst ever for aircraft losses and for loss of life. At 1,597 passenger deaths in aviation accidents, 1996 was the second worst year on record.
Merchant ship losses (over 500 gross tons) in 1996 are expected to rise to more than 120 from the current figure of 105, as more vessels are declared total losses or constructive total losses.
These figures compare with initial losses of 95 merchant ships in 1995, a figure which has since risen to 112.
The ILU described losses in 1995 as abnormally low, noting that 1996 losses were also lower than 1993 and earlier years.

"This may be for two reasons. First, much older tonnage has been scrapped recently, and, second, with ship values remaining high in most sectors it has been worth repairing more serious casualties than when values are low."
Although the number of ships lost last year was higher than in 1995, the total tonnage fell to 653,775 gross tons from 693,433 in 1995.
However, the number of lives lost was 1,190, compared with 316 in 1995, reflecting the number cruise liner and ferry accidents.
Space losses total a provisional $419 million. The year saw four significant satellite losses, the ILU said.
